§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.
--- Page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.
--- Page 3 ---
§4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

Classification is made by the Manager, Distribution Protection Engineering, on receipt of Form ER-11.
Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.
Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.
§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.
The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.
Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.

§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.
--- Page 2 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline Page 2
Factor definitions:
 Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
designation on the interconnection application.
 Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
 Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
verification, controls.
 Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
evidenced by the source documents in §3.
§3  DOCUMENTATION
For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system
of record:
 Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
 Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
 Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).
 Devices required to energize (RTU, POI recloser, or both), quantities, and specification references
(Standards Engineering).
 Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
 Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
attached by reference (customer submission).
 Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
reference (application file).
 Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not q

nks (1) or (2) are ranked by (3) with (4) as tiebreaker. The worksheet, the ranked deployment list, and
the assigned equipment-set identifiers shall be retained in the DER Program equipment-planning file for
the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.

Amendments to the worksheet arising after issuance — for example, receipt of previously missing
documentation for a listed site, or arrival of a new site into the waiting population — shall be recorded in an
addendum bearing its own date; prior ranked lists are not overwritten.
§4  VENDOR ENGAGEMENT EXPECTATIONS
Distribution Operations, working through Supply Chain, shall maintain rolling engagement with the current
approved suppliers of RTUs and POI reclosers with the following expectations:
 Lead-time visibility. A monthly written statement of committed lead times, next scheduled delivery
date, and delivery quantity per device type, retained in the equipment-planning file. Any change to a
previously committed date or quantity is to be flagged in writing on receipt.
 Order coverage. Standing purchase orders shall cover no fewer than the number of device sets
required to satisfy the sites eligible under §1 for the current deployment window plus the next
scheduled delivery window. Expedite requests shall be pursued where a delivery-date change would
displace a rank-(1) or rank-(2) site.
 Alternate sourcing. Where committed lead times exceed the interval between deliveries, Supply
Chain shall document the shortcoming of the current approved suppliers and evaluate qualification of
additional vendors under Standards Engineering's certification procedures. Qualification effort shall
not condition or delay deployment decisions for the current window.
 Substitution. Any proposed substitution of device model or configuration relative to the site's
approved specification is routed to Standards Engineering; substitutions are not accepted on
schedule pressure alone.
 Escrow / spares. A minimum spare quantity per device type shall be held at the operations
warehouse, replenished on drawdown, and not consumed to accelerate a lower-ranked site ahead of
a higher-ranked site whose device set is en route.
Vendor engagement records are subject to audit by Regulatory Affairs on request.
§5  COORDINATION WITH THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS CENTER
The ranked deployment list issued under §3 is transmitted to the SOC concurrent with its issuance.
Coordination steps are as follows:
 Pre-deployment briefing. For each device set scheduled to arrive in the deployment window, the
DER Program Office and the SOC Shift Supervisor confirm the receiving site, the anticipated
field-installation window, the commissioning sequence, and the telemetry integration steps required
for permission-to-operate (PTO). Nothing in this guideline modifies the SOC's PTO gating criteria;
TCS-02 §5 requires utility-owned RTU and SCADA telemetry with live telemetry established prior to
PTO for sites at or above 500 kW, and this guideline does not authorize interim or provisional
energization ahead of that condition.
 Change control. A change to the ranked list after transmittal to the SOC — for example, arrival of a
new rank-(1) site, or documented lapse of a committed deadline previously credited at rank (2) — is
issued by written addendum jointly to Supply Chain and to the SOC. Verbal reprioritization is not to be
relied upon.
 Field constraints. Where feeder condition, crew availability, or outage-window constraints prevent
installation at a higher-ranked site within the window, the SOC records the constraint and the DER
Program Office reissues the deployment assignment for that device set to the next-eligible site; the

higher-ranked site retains its rank for the following window.
 Commissioning readiness. The SOC's PTO-hold log continues to govern which completed sites are
eligible for energization steps; sites without established telemetry remain on the hold log until the
utility-owned RTU is installed and telemetry is verified in accordance with TCS-02.
 Reporting. A written record of device-set assignments, installation dates, commissioning outcomes,
and any addenda issued during the window is retained by the DER Program Office and made

SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
SUPPLEMENTAL REVIEW PROCEDURE
Doc no. Rev Effective date Owner
SRP-3 Rev 3 02/10/2025 Alleniom Standards Engineering
Supersedes: SRP-3 Rev 2 (effective 07/22/2022)
Classification: Technical Standard — Distributed Energy Resource Interconnection
Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; Distribution Planning; Standards Engineering;
Regulatory Affairs
§1   Purpose
This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.
Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
judgment.
Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.
§2   Scope
This procedure applies to:
(a)  all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and
(b)  all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
MW – 5 MW).
This procedure does not apply to:
(a)  sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;
(b)  capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
governed by DIS-01 §7; or
(c)  domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.
Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.
§3   Screens
--- Page 2 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering Page 2
Applications entering supplemental review shall be evaluated under the following screens, in the order given. An
application that fails any screen shall be considered a candidate for a study agreement; the reviewing engineer
shall document the failing screen, the underlying data, and the recommended disposition per §6.
Screen A — Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder. Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus
requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Queue
positions are those on record with the DER Program Office at the date of screen evaluation.
Screen B — Voltage regulation and flicker. Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where
none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation
performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record.
Screen C — Short-circuit contribution. DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective
device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to
fall below the values specified in DPS-07.
Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. Governed by §4.
Screen E — Reverse power flow at substation. Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the
substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in
place, the application shall be routed to study.
Passing all applicable screens is a necessary but not sufficient condition for interconnection; the application
remains subject to the balance of the DIS-01 evaluation, including protection and telemetry requirements.
§4   100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. For solar DER, the minimum load used in this screen shall be the
minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data. The absolute
overnight minimum shall NOT be used. Requested DER capacity must be ≤ this daytime-window minimum for
the site to pass the screen.
The daytime-window minimum shall be computed from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent
complete twelve (12) calendar months, aggregated to fifteen-minute intervals aligned to the feeder AMI
collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time
on the feeder. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching shall be excluded
and the exclusion documented in the reviewer's worksheet. Where fewer than twelve (12) months of AMI interval
data are available, the reviewer shall use the longest continuous complete period available and note the
data-window length in the supplemental review memo.
The daytime-window minimum determined under this section is the sole minimum-load figure used for the solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen. Feeder minimum-load figures produced for other purposes — planning studies,
hosting-capacity map inputs, protection coordination — are not substitutes for the value computed under this
section and shall not be carried into the Screen D determination without recomputation on the AMI record.
Where a prior supplemental review memo on the same feeder has applied a different minimum-load basis, the
reviewer shall recompute the value under this section and, if the two disagree, supersede the earlier memo in the
file.
§5   Data sources
The following data sources are authoritative for supplemental review under this procedure:
--- Page 3 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering Page 3
(a)  Feeder AMI interval data — from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse, at the meter aggregation level
published for the subject feeder. AMI interval data is the sole authoritative source for the Screen D
minimum-load determination described in §4.
(b)  Distribution planning record — most recent feeder planning study, conductor and transformer impedance
data, and protection coordination settings, held by Distribution Planning.
(c)  DER queue — active-queue and on-hold registers maintained by the DER Program Office as of the screen
evaluation date. Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen
A.
(d)  Certified Equipment List (CEL) — current edition, for verification that proposed inverters and PCS
equipment are eligible to be considered under the screens.
(e)  Interconnection application record — the applicant's filed capacity, single-line diagram, inverter
specifications, and control narrative (where controlled-capacity operation is asserted under DIS-01 §3.6).
Substitution of a source not listed above shall be documented in the memo produced under §6, together with the
reason for the substitution.
§6   Documentation
The reviewing engineer shall produce a supplemental review memo for each application processed under this
procedure. The memo shall contain, at minimum:
(a)  application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity;
(b)  the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each;
(c)  for Screen D, the daytime-window minimum load determined per §4, the data window used, the count of
intervals evaluated, and any interval exclusions with reason;
(d)  the recommended disposition — advance without study agreement, advance to study agreement, or return to
applicant with specified deficiency;
(e)  reviewer signature and date; and
(f)  the identifiers of any earlier supplemental review memos superseded.
The memo shall be filed to the interconnection application record within five (5) business days of screen
completion. Where a memo supersedes an earlier determination on the same application or the same feeder, the
superseded memo shall be flagged in the file and a cross-reference to the superseding memo added to its cover.

Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
Doc no. POL-QM-05  ·  Rev 3  ·  Date 03/15/2025  ·  Owner: DER Program Office
Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.
§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)	applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)	queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)	staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)	the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)	the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)	the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)	a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)	be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)	be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)	identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)	state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.	Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.	Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.	Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.	On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
5.	Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)	The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)	The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)	The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)	Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date in

7647 bytes
 permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)	the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)	at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)	the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)	be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)	be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)	identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)	state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)	state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)	state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)	“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)	Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)	The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
(d)	Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)	mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)	record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
(c)	preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
§3.6  Effect of Timely Response
A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
§3.7  Non-Substitution
Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
§4  Record-Keeping Requirements
§4.1  Case File Contents
For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
(a)	the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
(b)	for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
(c)	for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any response received;
(d)	the queue-management system entry recording the closure basis, closure date, and (for §2 duplicate-filing cases) the queue-date determination applied to the successor application under §2.4(a); and
(e)	any related engineering or standards correspondence relied upon in the closure decision.
§4.2  Queue-Management System Entries
Every closure shall be recorded in the queue-management system with:
(a)	application identifier and site;
(b)	closure basis, expressed as one of: “§2 — customer request (letter)”, “§2 — customer request (email)”, “§2.4 — superseded by successor application”, “§12.4 — deemed withdrawn”, or such other codes as the DER Program Office may prescribe;
(c)	closure date;
(d)	case handler; and
(e)	reference to the writing(s) supporting the closure basis.
§4.3  Withdrawal-Notice Log
The DER Program Office shall maintain a running Withdrawal-Notice Log recording every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation issued. The log shall include, at minimum: application identifier; site; date of issuance; method of service; response deadline (computed under §3.4); response received (date and disposition, if any); and closure date (if any). The log is subject to periodic reconciliation against the on-hold queue report; unreconciled entries shall be brought to the attention of the Manager, Interconnection Studies.
§4.4  Retention
Case files and log entries shall be retained in accordance with the Company's records retention schedule for regulated interconnection records. Records shall not be purged, redacted, or altered while an application remains open, while a response window under §3 is running, or while the closure is within the period during which reconsideration may be sought.
§4.5  Audit and Reporting
The Manager, Interconnection Studies shall be prepared, on request of Regulatory Affairs, to produce for any closed application: the closure basis; the writing(s) supporting the closure basis; the queue-date determination for any successor application; and, where applicable, the notice, proof of service, and 30 business-day computation. Reports to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission concerning queue closures shall be prepared from the withdrawal-notice log and the queue-management system entries described above.

Site: Prairie Corridor Business Park PV (PXA-2024-0343), POI recloser PC-POI-R1 with control NPC-38.

To be performed after installation and witnessed by Alleniom Utilities; results recorded on this form at the test.
Steps
Step 1 Insulation and dielectric. Measure insulation resistance of primary and secondary circuits at 5 kV DC for

Step 2 Instrument transformers. Verify CT ratio 200:5, polarity and burden; verify VT ratio 7200:120 V and

metering at the SCADA operator display against the RTU point table SCADA-PC-RTU-CFG-01.

element permits the close; close from the control cabinet and confirm the recloser closes. Open the recloser,
open the upstream line disconnect to de-energize the line side, and confirm a close command is refused. Trip
the recloser by secondary injection on the 27 element and confirm it goes to lockout with 79 blocked; confirm
the lockout holds until the operator release. Restore the line side, wait the stable-source time of settings sheet
Rev A (5 minutes), release, and confirm the close through 25.

confirm the clearance hold.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
--- Page 2 ---
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office Page 2
5. The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:
 the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
 for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;
--- Page 3 ---
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office Page 3
 for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;
 the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;
 correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.
End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards
Engineering and take effect on the date shown in the document-control block above.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PLANNING GROUP
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
System Impact Study Report
Doc no. Rev Date Owner
SIS-2025-006 Rev 0 06/22/2025 DER Planning Group
Project: PXA-2024-0343, Prairie Corridor Business Park PV, 860 kW AC. Customer: Prairie Corridor Partners
LLC. Site: 2200 Corridor Parkway, Halston, Alleron 05HA. Feeder ALN-088 (13.2 kV).
Study type: SIS (small). Prepared by Devon Reyes, DER Planning Group; reviewed by Ivo Grantham, Manager,
DER Planning Group. Study start 02/03/2025; complete 06/22/2025.
1. Facility description
The array is installed on the rooftops of the park's four buildings: six Solmery inverters in three blocks (two
SM-245K-3P in block 1, two SM-125K-3P in block 2, two SM-60K-3P in block 3), 860 kW AC in total. The
inverters connect to the park's 480 V distribution and reach the feeder through the park's existing 13.2 kV
primary service and revenue meter M-1. The array sits behind the meter at that service, so the park's tenant
load is served first and the surplus is exported at the point of interconnection.
Park demand at the service, from 12 months of AMI interval data at meter M-1 (calendar 2024): weekday
daytime (10:00 to 16:00) 410 to 620 kW; weekend daytime 170 to 260 kW; annual peak 744 kW (08/14/2024,
15:00).
2. Assumptions
Export at the point of interconnection was studied at 860 kW with zero park load, the bounding case for voltage
rise and reverse power flow. Fault contribution was taken at 1.1 per unit of inverter rated current. Anti-islanding
is by the inverters' UL 1741-SB active scheme (all six models are carried on CEL-2025-Q2).
3. Results
Screen Result Basis
Steady-state voltage at POI, full export,
light load
1.031 pu (limit 1.05 pu) DIS-01 Rev 4
Voltage change on loss of full output 2.1 percent (limit 3 percent) DIS-01 Rev 4
Thermal loading, ALN-088 trunk 71 percent of rating at full
export
Feeder model 2025-01
Fault current contribution at POI 41 A (three-phase) 1.1 pu inverter current
Islanding non-detection zone not identified; DTT not required DPS-07 §4.5, §5.3
4. Conditions of interconnection
4.1 Utility-owned POI recloser per DPS-07 §4.2, with settings issued by Distribution Protection Engineering
under DPS-07 §5.5. Automatic reclosing at the POI recloser to be blocked, with the recloser locked out on loss
of the utility source per DPS-07 §5.1(b); synchronism check (25) to supervise closing.
4.2 Upstream feeder recloser ALN-088 R2: first reclose interval raised from 0.5 s to 2.0 s so the POI recloser
opens on loss of source before the first reclose attempt (DPS-07 §5.1(a)).
4.3 Directional power element (32) at the POI recloser applied as an export backstop at 900 kW, 2.0 s.
4.4 Utility-owned RTU and SCADA telemetry per TCS-02, including the §6.1 points, ahead of Permission to
Operate (TCS-02 §5).
4.5 Protection coordination study and sign-off by Distribution Protection Engineering before energization
(DPS-07 §5.1(c)).
5. Status
Study complete 06/22/2025. Conditions 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5 pass to Distribution Protection Engineering; 4.2 to
Distribution Operations; 4.4 to SCADA/EMS Engineering.
Devon Reyes, DER Planning Group, 06/22/2025.

# NEC Chapter 9 Table 4: 2 in. RMC (Rigid Metal Conduit):
# Internal diameter = 2.083 in., Total Area (100%) = 3.408 in^2, 40% fill (over 2 conductors) = 1.363 in^2.
# What is the area of 4/0 AWG and 4 AWG in NEC Chapter 9 Table 5?
# For RHW-2 / RHH / USE-2 (without outer covering, 600V-2000V):
# Wait: 4/0 AWG RHH/RHW/RHW-2 (600V): area = 0.3718 in^2 (or THHN = 0.3237 in^2, XHHW = 0.3197 in^2)
# 4/0 AWG RHH/RHW-2 2000V: approx 0.45-0.55 in^2
# For 1 circuit (2 x 4/0 + 1 x 4 AWG): 2 * 0.3718 + 0.1333 = 0.8769 in^2 <= 1.363 in^2 (25.7% fill, easily passes!)
# For 2 circuits (4 x 4/0 + 1 x 4 AWG): 4 * 0.3718 + 0.1333 = 1.6205 in^2 > 1.363 in^2!
print("1 circuit (RHW-2 600V):", 2*0.3718 + 0.1333, "vs 1.363 (40% of 3.408)")
print("2 circuits (RHW-2 600V):", 4*0.3718 + 0.1333, "vs 1.363 (40% of 3.408)")
print("2 circuits (THHN):", 4*0.3237 + 0.0824, "vs 1.363 (40% of 3.408)")
'

Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.

Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.

A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.

items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.

2. Screen applied
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar, per §4 of SRP-3 (Rev 3, effective 02/10/2025). Under this screen, the requested DER capacity is compared against the minimum load observed on the subject feeder from AMI interval data.
3. Analysis
Reviewed AMI interval load data for Feeder ALN-214 from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse and identified a minimum feeder load of 1.1 MW. The value was drawn from the feeder AMI record available on file for ALN-214. No intervals were excluded for known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching during the period reviewed.
4. Comparison
1.8 MW requested exceeds 1.1 MW minimum feeder load — screen FAILED.
5. Recommendation
Study Agreement required prior to advancement. The application should not proceed on the supplemental-review track. A Study Agreement should be offered to Bramwick Commons Solar LLC, with the scope covering the technical conditions that gave rise to the failed screen on Feeder ALN-214.
6. Disposition
Return supplemental review file to Interconnection Studies queue with a failed-screen flag on Feeder ALN-214.
Notify the applicant of the screen result and forward the Study Agreement package.
Hold advancement of PXA record for Bramwick Commons Solar until Study Agreement is executed.

P19: 3. Items on the 07/14/2025 Record Standing in the Way of Permission to Operate
P20: Outside the four excluded matters in Section 2, the following items on the record as of 07/14/2025 stand in the way of issuing Permission to Operate and must be settled before PTO can issue on 08/04/2025:
P21: Item 1 — Utility RTU Station AC Service (PP-1 Circuit 1 / TX-1) and Inverter Control Power Connected Behind the Open POI Recloser
P22: (1) What the Issue Is: On Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (Drawing E-101 Rev C, 06/24/2025), the 15 kVA auxiliary transformer TX-1 (480 V to 120/240 V) is fed from a 40 A two-pole breaker in the PV switchboard SWBD-PV, and auxiliary panel PP-1 (120/240 V, fed from TX-1) supplies Circuit 1—the dedicated 20 A station AC service circuit to the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole (through the 1.5 kVA online UPS in that enclosure, stated as 5.5 h at the RTU load)—as well as Circuit 2 (SWBD-PV enclosure heaters, 20 A). In addition, E-101 Rev C specifies that the five inverters (INV-C1 to INV-C5) derive their 'control power internal, from the inverter's own ac output terminals.' Because SWBD-PV is connected to Feeder ALN-072 through step-up transformer T-1 (750 kVA) and primary switch PSW-1 on the customer/load side of the utility's POI recloser (ISA Exhibit A, Exhibit B §B.2), SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 are energized ONLY when the POI recloser is closed. On 07/08/2025, the POI recloser was closed from 08:10 to 15:35 under Distribution Operations switching order DO-2025-0677 for the witness test (WT-0629-01), which energized SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 and allowed SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and the SOC Shift Supervisor (Lena Kovalchuk) to confirm live telemetry on 07/08/2025 (CX-CW-01 Rev 2). However, at 15:35 on 07/08/2025, Distribution Operations opened the POI recloser locally (WT-0629-01), and ISA §6.1 mandates that '[a]t all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.' With the POI recloser open, T-1, SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 are completely de-energized (and the inverters cannot energize a dead island and have no AC voltage at their output terminals for internal control power). Once the 1.5 kVA UPS battery in the RTU enclosure discharged after 5.5 hours on the evening of 07/08/2025, the utility RTU lost all station power. Consequently, while the POI recloser remains open before PTO per ISA §6.1, the utility RTU has no station AC power and cannot present live, valid telemetry at the SCADA display at the moment PTO is issued (TCS-02 §5(c); ISA §6.2, §7.2) or provide active SCADA supervision of the POI recloser for first parallel operation (ISA §6.3; DPS-07 §6.3). Furthermore, after PTO, any POI recloser trip to lockout (DPS-07 §5.1(b); ISA §8.3–§8.4) or customer clearance on PSW-1 or SWBD-PV (ISA §8.5) lasting longer than the UPS battery runtime will de-energize the utility RTU (defeating remote SCADA supervision and reconnection) and de-energize the SWBD-PV anti-condensation enclosure heaters when the switchboard is offline.
P23: (2) What It Rests On: ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §5.2 (customer provides station service for the RTU), §6.1 (POI recloser kept open at all times before PTO except during witness test), §6.2 (live telemetry at SOC required for PTO), §6.3 (first parallel operation observed by SOC with POI recloser under SCADA supervision), §7.2 (customer provisions for RTU and live telemetry per TCS-02 §5), §8.3–§8.5 (disconnection, SOC release for reconnection, and clearances); TCS-02 Rev 1 §3.1, §3.4 (customer-provided dedicated branch circuit for station AC service to RTU enclosure), §4.3, and §5(c) (RTU must present all required points as valid at the SCADA operator display at the moment PTO is issued); DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2(4) (remote operation and monitoring via SCADA per TCS-02), §5.1(b) (recloser lockout and operator-supervised reconnection), and §6.3; DIS-01 Rev 4 §6; Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (tags TX-1, PP-1, INV-C1 to INV-C5); Witness Test Record WT-0629-01 (07/08/2025).
P24: (3) What Has to Be Done About It and By Whom: Corwyn Realty Partners (through its electrical contractor, Brantley Electric Company, Lic. #EC-12306) must re-feed the dedicated 120 V, 20 A station AC service branch circuit to the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole (and SWBD-PV enclosure heaters / inverter control power if continuous inverter communication is required while isolated) from a permanent, continuously energized AC source on the premises that is independent of the POI recloser and SWBD-PV—specifically from the Corwyn Office Complex parking-structure ground-floor electrical room panel LP-2 (which already supplies monitoring cabinet DAS-1 per E-401 Rev C) or an independent utility-side/building auxiliary service—issue a revised Equipment Schedule (E-101 Rev D), and obtain supplemental inspection sign-off from the City of Wrenford Department of Inspections (Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector) under Permit WEP-25-0317. Alleniom Utilities — SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and the System Operations Center (Lena Kovalchuk) must then verify continuous 120 V AC station service at the RTU enclosure and live, valid SCADA telemetry while the POI recloser is open.
P25: (4) Whether That Can Be Done Before 08/04/2025: YES. Twenty-one (21) calendar days (15 business days) remain between 07/14/2025 and 08/04/2025. Extending/re-terminating a 120 V, 20 A branch circuit from the adjacent parking structure electrical room (panel LP-2) to feed the RTU auxiliary circuit, updating Drawing E-101, obtaining local City of Wrenford electrical inspection approval, and re-verifying live SCADA telemetry require approximately 3 to 5 business days and can be completed well before 08/04/2025.
P26: Item 2 — Per-Inverter Telemetry Refresh Rate (5 Minutes vs. ≤ 4 Seconds) on Monitoring & Communications Schedule E-401 Rev C
P27: (1) What the Issue Is: Monitoring and Communications Schedule E-401 Rev C (Drawing E-401 Rev C, 06/24/2025) defines both the customer's DAS-1 cabinet and 'the inverters' data link to the utility RTU (ISA §7.2)' (link COM-RTU, which connects INV-C1 to INV-C5 RS-485 port 2 on one multi-drop bus to the utility RTU serial port on the POI pole for 'per-inverter ac power and status for SCADA'). On the 'Points' sheet of E-401 Rev C, the reporting interval for 'AC power, energy, voltage and current per inverter' (Source: INV-C1 to INV-C5) is specified as '5 min' (300 seconds), with 'Inverter status and fault codes' specified as 'On change.' Under TCS-02 §6.1, where a site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks behind a common POI, values must be reported both individually per block and as a facility total, including the analog point 'Gross generation (per inverter block) kW' and the status point 'Inverter/PCS block status (Per block: run, standby, fault).' Under TCS-02 §6.2 (Refresh rates), analog values must be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds (using DNP3 Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than every 60 seconds), and status points by exception on change of state with an integrity poll no less frequently than every 60 seconds; only cumulative energy registers (kWh) are permitted on a 5-minute cycle ('no less frequently than every five (5) minutes'). A 5-minute interval for per-inverter AC power on the COM-RTU link violates TCS-02 §6.2 and ISA §7.2.
P28: (2) What It Rests On: ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §4.1, §6.2, §7.2 (customer makes available the analog and status points that TCS-02 requires); TCS-02 Rev 1 §3.3(a) (RTU polls inverter/PCS at the refresh cadence specified in §6), §5(b)–(c) (communicating with SCADA at the refresh cadence required by §6), §6.1 (Required data points: Gross generation per inverter block in kW, Inverter/PCS block status), §6.2 (Refresh rates: ≤ 4 s for analog values, ≤ 60 s integrity poll for analog and status points, ≤ 5 min for cumulative energy registers), and §6.3 (Data quality); DIS-01 Rev 4 §6; Monitoring and Communications Schedule E-401 Rev C (Header, Links, Points).
P29: (3) What Has to Be Done About It and By Whom: Corwyn Realty Partners (through Brantley Electric Company and Vexlar Energy field service) must verify/configure the INV-C1 to INV-C5 RS-485 port 2 (COM-RTU) register polling/reporting interface and issue a revised Monitoring and Communications Schedule (E-401 Rev D) so that per-inverter analog points (Gross generation per inverter block, kW) are available and updated to the utility RTU at intervals ≤ 4 seconds (and Class 0 integrity poll ≤ 60 seconds for analog and status points), while applying the 5-minute interval only to cumulative energy registers (kWh) and customer DAS-1 logging on RS-485 port 1. Alleniom Utilities — SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and the System Operations Center (Lena Kovalchuk) must verify the ≤ 4-second per-inverter analog update cadence at SCADA.
P30: (4) Whether That Can Be Done Before 08/04/2025: YES. Adjusting the RS-485 port 2 polling/reporting rate and issuing revised Drawing E-401 Rev D is a configuration and documentation task requiring 1 to 2 business days and can be completed well before 08/04/2025.
P31: Item 3 — Utility RTU Enclosure 1.5 kVA Online UPS 4-Hour Outage Ride-Through Under Cold-Ambient (< 10 °C) and End-of-Life Derating
P32: (1) What the Issue Is: Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (tag PP-1) states that Circuit 1 supplies the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole 'through the 1.5 kVA online UPS in that enclosure (5.5 h at the RTU load).' Under TCS-02 §3.4, the uninterruptible power supply must be sized for a minimum four (4) hour outage ride-through. The 1.5 kVA online UPS specification on file (Corvane Power Systems OL-1500R, Document OL1500R-DS Rev 4, 03/2024: 1500 VA / 1350 W, 4 × 12 V 9 Ah VRLA = 432 Wh nominal, 376 Wh usable battery energy at 25 °C new battery, 88% battery-mode inverter efficiency, 40 W online standing loss) explicitly requires: 'Derate 20 percent at end of battery life and below 10 degC.' Because the RTU enclosure is mounted outdoors on the POI pole in Wrenford, Alleron (where ambient temperatures fall below 10 °C, with a site design low temperature of -24 °C per E-301 Rev C), the 20% derating factor (0.80) applies: Runtime_derated = 0.80 × 376 Wh / (P_load / 0.88 + 40 W). Under this governing formula, achieving ≥ 4.0 hours of derated runtime requires the total continuous load on the UPS output to be ≤ 30.98 W (~31.0 W). A new-battery runtime of 5.5 h at 25 °C corresponds to a load of only ~25 W (or a miscalculation dividing 432 Wh nominal energy by 38 W RTU + 40 W standing loss = 5.54 h without usable-energy, inverter-efficiency, or 20% derating). At the standard Alleniom pole-mounted RTU + cellular modem load of 38 W + 12 W = 50 W, the Corvane OL-1500R provides only 3.88 hours new at 25 °C and 3.10 hours derated (and even for a 38 W RTU load alone, 4.52 hours new at 25 °C derates by 20% to 3.62 hours)—both below the 4.0-hour minimum mandated by TCS-02 §3.4.
P33: (2) What It Rests On: TCS-02 Rev 1 §3.4 (Environmental and station-service requirements: minimum 4-hour outage ride-through); ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §4.1, §5.2, §7.2; Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (tag PP-1); Corvane Power Systems OL-1500R Data Sheet (Document OL1500R-DS Rev 4, 03/2024).
P34: (3) What Has to Be Done About It and By Whom: Corwyn Realty Partners (with Brantley Electric Company) and Alleniom Utilities — SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) must verify and document the exact watt load connected to the UPS output in the POI pole RTU enclosure (confirming also that no enclosure heater is wired to the UPS battery output). P1: 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  der.program@alleniom.com  ·  alleniom.com
P2: ENGINEERING REVIEW MEMORANDUM — PERMISSION TO OPERATE DETERMINATION
P3: TO:	Lena Kovalchuk, SOC Shift Supervisor, System Operations Center (lena.kovalchuk@alleniom.com · (612) 555-0103)
P4: FROM:	Reviewing Engineer, P.E., DER Program Office (Tomás Ibarra, P.E., Sr. Interconnection Engineer, DER Program Office, Alleniom Utilities)
P5: CC:	S. Rennick, Commissioning Coordinator, DER Program Office; Evan Solberg, Standards Engineer; Marcus Deele, SCADA/EMS Engineering; Nolan Achterberg, P.E., Distribution Protection Engineering; Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies; Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group; Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs; Dana Whitcomb, VP, Distribution Operations
P6: DATE:	07/14/2025 (Record Anchor Date: 2025-07-14)
P7: SUBJECT:	Permission to Operate (PTO) Engineering Review and Determination — Corwyn Office Complex PV (Application PXA-2023-0629, Agreement ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, Feeder ALN-072, Requested PTO Date 08/04/2025 [2025-08-04])
P8: 1. Executive Determination and Summary of Basis
P9: A. Record-Date Posture as of 07/14/2025 (Immediate Release List: Empty / Zero — HOLD): Working strictly from the project record as it stands on 07/14/2025, Permission to Operate (PTO) for Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) CANNOT issue unconditionally on the unamended 07/14/2025 record. As of 07/14/2025, the list of facilities under this review that can be unconditionally released for PTO without prior curative action is empty (zero). If no corrective action is completed between 07/14/2025 and 08/04/2025, the System Operations Center (SOC) must HOLD Permission to Operate on 08/04/2025.
P10: B. Determination for Requested PTO Date of 08/04/2025 (Contingent Release Posture — CAN ISSUE on 08/04/2025 Upon Cure of Record Deficiencies): Every impediment standing in the way on the 07/14/2025 record (Items 1 through 5 in Section 3 below) CAN be remedied and verified well before the requested PTO date of 08/04/2025 (21 calendar days / 15 business days from 07/14/2025, requiring an estimated 3 to 5 business days of field, configuration, and documentation work). All long-lead contractual, equipment-allocation, construction, permitting, metering, and witness-test requirements are already satisfied on the record as of 07/14/2025. Therefore, Permission to Operate CAN ISSUE on 08/04/2025 if and only if Corwyn Realty Partners (with its contractor, Brantley Electric Company) and Alleniom Utilities settle Items 1 through 5 before 08/04/2025; otherwise, Lena Kovalchuk must HOLD PTO on 08/04/2025 until those items are settled.
P11: C. Summary of Basis: Under Article 6 (§6.1–§6.3) and Article 7 (§7.1–§7.2) of the executed Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, effective 09/12/2024), together with Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4 (§4–§6), Distribution Protection Standard DPS-07 Rev 2 (§4.2–§4.5, §5.1, §6.2–§6.3), Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02 Rev 1 (§3.1–§3.6, §5, §6.1–§6.3), Witness Test & Waiver Procedure ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 (§3, §4.1–§4.3), Certified Equipment List CEL-2025-Q2, and the 2023 National Electrical Code (NFPA 70, adopted by City of Wrenford Ordinance 24-118 under Permit WEP-25-0317), parallel operation may begin only upon written Permission to Operate issued once: (i) the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted, (ii) live telemetry is presenting all required data points as valid at the SOC SCADA display at the moment PTO is issued (TCS-02 §5(c)) and station service is compliant with TCS-02 §3.4, (iii) the on-site witness test is complete and passed, and (iv) the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) has given final approval of compliant customer facilities. While the contractual, permitting, metering, inverter certification, and witness-test records are complete as of 07/14/2025, engineering review of the customer's technical schedules (E-101 Rev C, E-201 Rev C, E-301 Rev C, and E-401 Rev C) and commissioning records (CX-CW-01 Rev 2 and WT-0629-01) identifies four technical/submittal impediments (Items 1–4) plus the mandatory day-of-PTO telemetry/supervision gate (Item 5) that stand in the way on the 07/14/2025 record.
P12: 2. Scope Exclusions (Four Matters Under Separate Review)
P13: Per program direction, the following four scope exclusions apply (Four matters are under separate review and are not for this memo: the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering); the POI recloser's settings and the protection coordination study behind them (Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records); the site's queue position (Meera Vellanki, under the weekly queue reports); and the system impact study and its conditions (Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records). Nothing else is under separate review.):
P14: 1. Installation, configuration, and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (under separate review by SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering) — 1. Company RTU and POI Recloser Installation, Configuration, and Commissioning Tests: The installation, configuration, and commissioning tests of Alleniom Utilities' remote terminal unit (RTU) and point-of-interconnection (POI) recloser at the site are under separate review by SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and Distribution Protection Engineering (Nolan Achterberg, P.E.).
P15: 2. POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study behind them (under separate review by Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records) — 2. POI Recloser Settings and Protection Coordination Study: The POI recloser's protective settings and the protection coordination study behind them (DPS-07 §5.1, §5.5) are under separate review by Distribution Protection Engineering (Nolan Achterberg, P.E.), which issued them on 06/18/2025 and maintains them outside these records.
P16: 3. The site's queue position (under separate review by Meera Vellanki under the weekly queue reports) — 3. Site Queue Position: The site's interconnection queue position (Application PXA-2023-0629, queue date 07/11/2023 on Feeder ALN-072) is under separate review by Meera Vellanki (Manager, Interconnection Studies) under the weekly queue reports.
P17: 4. The system impact study and its conditions (under separate review by Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records) — 4. System Impact Study and Conditions: The system impact study and its conditions for the facility are under separate review by Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which maintains them outside these records.
P18: Scope Completeness Rule: Nothing else is under separate review. All other aspects of the PXA-2023-0629 record as of 07/14/2025—including the executed ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, customer-owned interconnection and generating facilities, customer-furnished station service and telemetry provisions for the Company's RTU (ISA §5.2, §7.2; TCS-02 §3.1, §3.4, §5, §6), engineering schedules E-101 Rev C, E-201 Rev C, E-301 Rev C, and E-401 Rev C, CEL-2025-Q2 compliance, Certificate of Conformance VX-CC-25-0522, Witness Test Record WT-0629-01, Commissioning Checklist CX-CW-01 Rev 2, City of Wrenford Permit/Final Approval WEP-25-0317, and program hold/payment registers—are evaluated in this memorandum.
P19: 3. Items on the 07/14/2025 Record Standing in the Way of Permission to Operate
P20: Outside the four excluded matters in Section 2, the following items on the record as of 07/14/2025 stand in the way of issuing Permission to Operate and must be settled before PTO can issue on 08/04/2025:
P21: Item 1 — Utility RTU Station AC Service (PP-1 Circuit 1 / TX-1) and Inverter Control Power Connected Behind the Open POI Recloser
P22: (1) What the Issue Is: On Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (Drawing E-101 Rev C, 06/24/2025), the 15 kVA auxiliary transformer TX-1 (480 V to 120/240 V) is fed from a 40 A two-pole breaker in the PV switchboard SWBD-PV, and auxiliary panel PP-1 (120/240 V, fed from TX-1) supplies Circuit 1—the dedicated 20 A station AC service circuit to the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole (through the 1.5 kVA online UPS in that enclosure, stated as 5.5 h at the RTU load)—as well as Circuit 2 (SWBD-PV enclosure heaters, 20 A). In addition, E-101 Rev C specifies that the five inverters (INV-C1 to INV-C5) derive their 'control power internal, from the inverter's own ac output terminals.' Because SWBD-PV is connected to Feeder ALN-072 through step-up transformer T-1 (750 kVA) and primary switch PSW-1 on the customer/load side of the utility's POI recloser (ISA Exhibit A, Exhibit B §B.2), SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 are energized ONLY when the POI recloser is closed. On 07/08/2025, the POI recloser was closed from 08:10 to 15:35 under Distribution Operations switching order DO-2025-0677 for the witness test (WT-0629-01), which energized SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 and allowed SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and the SOC Shift Supervisor (Lena Kovalchuk) to confirm live telemetry on 07/08/2025 (CX-CW-01 Rev 2). However, at 15:35 on 07/08/2025, Distribution Operations opened the POI recloser locally (WT-0629-01), and ISA §6.1 mandates that '[a]t all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.' With the POI recloser open, T-1, SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 are completely de-energized (and the inverters cannot energize a dead island and have no AC voltage at their output terminals for internal control power). Once the 1.5 kVA UPS battery in the RTU enclosure discharged after 5.5 hours on the evening of 07/08/2025, the utility RTU lost

Under TCS-02 §6.1, where a site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks behind a common POI, values must be reported both individually per block and as a facility total, including the analog point 'Gross generation (per inverter block) kW' and the status point 'Inverter/PCS block status (Per block: run, standby, fault).' Under TCS-02 §6.2 (Refresh rates), analog values must be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds (using DNP3 Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than every 60 seconds), and status points by exception on change of state with an integrity poll no less frequently than every 60 seconds; only cumulative energy registers (kWh) are permitted on a 5-minute cycle ('no less frequently than every five (5) minutes'). Under TCS-02 §3.4, the uninterruptible power supply must be sized for a minimum four (4) hour outage ride-through. The 1.5 kVA online UPS specification on file (Corvane Power Systems OL-1500R, Document OL1500R-DS Rev 4, 03/2024: 1500 VA / 1350 W, 4 × 12 V 9 Ah VRLA = 432 Wh nominal, 376 Wh usable battery energy at 25 °C new battery, 88% battery-mode inverter efficiency, 40 W online standing loss) explicitly requires: 'Derate 20 percent at end of battery life and below 10 degC.' Because the RTU enclosure is mounted outdoors on the POI pole in Wrenford, Alleron (where ambient temperatures fall below 10 °C, with a site design low temperature of -24 °C per E-301 Rev C), the 20% derating factor (0.80) applies: Runtime_derated = 0.80 × 376 Wh / (P_load / 0.88 + 40 W). Under this governing formula, achieving ≥ 4.0 hours of derated runtime requires the total continuous load on the UPS output to be ≤ 30.98 W (~31.0 W). A new-battery runtime of 5.5 h at 25 °C corresponds to a load of only ~25 W (or a miscalculation dividing 432 Wh nominal energy by 38 W RTU + 40 W standing loss = 5.54 h without usable-energy, inverter-efficiency, or 20% derating).
