P19: 3. Items on the 07/14/2025 Record Standing in the Way of Permission to Operate

P20: Outside the four excluded matters in Section 2, the following items on the record as of 07/14/2025 stand in the way of issuing Permission to Operate and must be settled before PTO can issue on 08/04/2025:

P21: Item 1 — Utility RTU Station AC Service (PP-1 Circuit 1 / TX-1) and Inverter Control Power Connected Behind the Open POI Recloser

P22: (1) What the Issue Is: On Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (Drawing E-101 Rev C, 06/24/2025), the 15 kVA auxiliary transformer TX-1 (480 V to 120/240 V) is fed from a 40 A two-pole breaker in the PV switchboard SWBD-PV, and auxiliary panel PP-1 (120/240 V, fed from TX-1) supplies Circuit 1—the dedicated 20 A station AC service circuit to the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole (through the 1.5 kVA online UPS in that enclosure, stated as 5.5 h at the RTU load)—as well as Circuit 2 (SWBD-PV enclosure heaters, 20 A). In addition, E-101 Rev C specifies that the five inverters (INV-C1 to INV-C5) derive their 'control power internal, from the inverter's own ac output terminals.' Because SWBD-PV is connected to Feeder ALN-072 through step-up transformer T-1 (750 kVA) and primary switch PSW-1 on the customer/load side of the utility's POI recloser (ISA Exhibit A, Exhibit B §B.2), SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 are energized ONLY when the POI recloser is closed. On 07/08/2025, the POI recloser was closed from 08:10 to 15:35 under Distribution Operations switching order DO-2025-0677 for the witness test (WT-0629-01), which energized SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 and allowed SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and the SOC Shift Supervisor (Lena Kovalchuk) to confirm live telemetry on 07/08/2025 (CX-CW-01 Rev 2). However, at 15:35 on 07/08/2025, Distribution Operations opened the POI recloser locally (WT-0629-01), and ISA §6.1 mandates that '[a]t all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.' With the POI recloser open, T-1, SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 are completely de-energized (and the inverters cannot energize a dead island and have no AC voltage at their output terminals for internal control power). Once the 1.5 kVA UPS battery in the RTU enclosure discharged after 5.5 hours on the evening of 07/08/2025, the utility RTU lost all station power. Consequently, while the POI recloser remains open before PTO per ISA §6.1, the utility RTU has no station AC power and cannot present live, valid telemetry at the SCADA display at the moment PTO is issued (TCS-02 §5(c); ISA §6.2, §7.2) or provide active SCADA supervision of the POI recloser for first parallel operation (ISA §6.3; DPS-07 §6.3). Furthermore, after PTO, any POI recloser trip to lockout (DPS-07 §5.1(b); ISA §8.3–§8.4) or customer clearance on PSW-1 or SWBD-PV (ISA §8.5) lasting longer than the UPS battery runtime will de-energize the utility RTU (defeating remote SCADA supervision and reconnection) and de-energize the SWBD-PV anti-condensation enclosure heaters when the switchboard is offline.

P31: Item 3 — Utility RTU Enclosure 1.5 kVA Online UPS 4-Hour Outage Ride-Through Under Cold-Ambient (< 10 °C) and End-of-Life Derating

P32: (1) What the Issue Is: Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (tag PP-1) states that Circuit 1 supplies the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole 'through the 1.5 kVA online UPS in that enclosure (5.5 h at the RTU load).' Under TCS-02 §3.4, the uninterruptible power supply must be sized for a minimum four (4) hour outage ride-through. The 1.5 kVA online UPS specification on file (Corvane Power Systems OL-1500R, Document OL1500R-DS Rev 4, 03/2024: 1500 VA / 1350 W, 4 × 12 V 9 Ah VRLA = 432 Wh nominal, 376 Wh usable battery energy at 25 °C new battery, 88% battery-mode inverter efficiency, 40 W online standing loss) explicitly requires: 'Derate 20 percent at end of battery life and below 10 degC.' Because the RTU enclosure is mounted outdoors on the POI pole in Wrenford, Alleron (where ambient temperatures fall below 10 °C, with a site design low temperature of -24 °C per E-301 Rev C), the 20% derating factor (0.80) applies: Runtime_derated = 0.80 × 376 Wh / (P_load / 0.88 + 40 W). Under this governing formula, achieving ≥ 4.0 hours of derated runtime requires the total continuous load on the UPS output to be ≤ 30.98 W (~31.0 W). A new-battery runtime of 5.5 h at 25 °C corresponds to a load of only ~25 W (or a miscalculation dividing 432 Wh nominal energy by 38 W RTU + 40 W standing loss = 5.54 h without usable-energy, inverter-efficiency, or 20% derating). At the standard Alleniom pole-mounted RTU + cellular modem load of 38 W + 12 W = 50 W, the Corvane OL-1500R provides only 3.88 hours new at 25 °C and 3.10 hours derated (and even for a 38 W RTU load alone, 4.52 hours new at 25 °C derates by 20% to 3.62 hours)—both below the 4.0-hour minimum mandated by TCS-02 §3.4.

P33: (2) What It Rests On: TCS-02 Rev 1 §3.4 (Environmental and station-service requirements: minimum 4-hour outage ride-through); ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §4.1, §5.2, §7.2; Equipment Schedule E-101 Rev C (tag PP-1); Corvane Power Systems OL-1500R Data Sheet (Document OL1500R-DS Rev 4, 03/2024).

P34: (3) What Has to Be Done About It and By Whom: Corwyn Realty Partners (with Brantley Electric Company) and Alleniom Utilities — SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) must verify and document the exact watt load connected to the UPS output in the POI pole RTU enclosure (confirming also that no enclosure heater is wired to the UPS battery output). If the connected RTU and communications load exceeds 31.0 W (e.g., 38 W RTU + 12 W modem = 50 W), Corwyn Realty Partners / Brantley Electric Company must install an external battery pack or higher-capacity UPS providing ≥ 4.0 hours of ride-through after the 20% cold-temperature/end-of-life derating (at least 484 Wh usable energy at 25 °C for a 50 W load) and update E-101 Rev D.

=== ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex_Executed_Agreement.docx ===
INTERCONNECTION SERVICE AGREEMENT
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex · Rev Final · Date 09/12/2024 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts
Agreement No.: ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex
Project: Corwyn Office Complex PV
Application No.: PXA-2023-0629
This Interconnection Service Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (the "Company"), and Corwyn Realty Partners, with offices at 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR (the "Interconnection Customer"), each a "Party" and together the "Parties." This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.
RECITALS
WHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2023-0629, on 07/11/2023, for a 700 kW (ac) photovoltaic generating facility on five parking canopies at the Corwyn Office Complex, to be interconnected to the Company's distribution system on Feeder ALN-072;
WHEREAS, the Company completed its review of the application under the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and approved the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in this Agreement;
WHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms part of the terms of interconnection service under this Agreement;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Company's filed tariff (the "Tariff") and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the "DIS").
1.2 "Facility" means the generating facility described in Exhibit B: the five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, one on each of the five parking canopies, together with the Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B.
1.3 "Point of Interconnection" or "POI" means the point on Feeder ALN-072 at which the Facility connects to the Company's distribution system, at the Company's POI recloser in the north lot. The point of common coupling coincides with the Point of Interconnection.
1.4 "Company's Facilities" means the POI recloser, the remote terminal unit (RTU) and revenue meter RM-0629 described in Article 5.
1.5 "Permission to Operate" means the Company's written permission for parallel operation of the Facility under Article 6.
1.6 "Standards" means the Company standards identified in Section 4.1.
ARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY
2.1 Project designation. Corwyn Office Complex PV (Application PXA-2023-0629).
2.2 Interconnection Customer. Corwyn Realty Partners.
2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation on five parking canopies over the surface lots beside the parking structure.
2.4 Capacity. 700 kW (ac), export at the Point of Interconnection.
2.5 Feeder. ALN-072, 13.2 kV.
2.6 Material terms. The capacity and the Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement (Tariff §12.6; DIS §7).
ARTICLE 3 — TERM
3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 09/12/2024, the date on which the last of the Parties executed it.
3.2 Term. This Agreement remains in force from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.
3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality and dispute resolution survive any termination of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 4 — STANDARDS
4.1 The Facility shall be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated and maintained in conformity with DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time.
4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency, the following order governs: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the Standards; (iii) the body of this Agreement and its Exhibits.
ARTICLE 5 — INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
5.1 Company's Facilities. The Company provides, owns and operates the POI recloser (DPS-07 §4.2), the RTU (TCS-02 §3) and revenue meter RM-0629 with 13.2 kV primary metering at the Point of Interconnection, at the Interconnection Customer's cost under the construction work order.
5.2 Interconnection Customer's facilities. The Interconnection Customer provides, owns and maintains the interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B and the site provisions for the Company's Facilities (equipment pad, primary conductors to the recloser terminals, and the station service and communications entrance for the RTU) as specified in the Company's construction package.
5.3 Access. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company access at all times to the Point of Interconnection, the revenue meter and the Facility's disconnects.
ARTICLE 6 — COMMISSIONING AND PERMISSION TO OPERATE
6.1 Witness test. Before permission to operate, the Company may place the Facility in parallel with its distribution system solely for the witness test of the Facility under the Company's Witness Test & Waiver Procedure, under a Distribution Operations switching order and with the System Operations Center observing. At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.
6.2 Permission to operate. Parallel operation begins only with the Company's written permission to operate, issued once the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted, telemetry is live at the System Operations Center, the witness test is complete, and the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities.
6.3 First parallel operation. The first parallel operation after permission to operate is observed by the System Operations Center with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision (DPS-07 §6.3).
ARTICLE 7 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
7.1 Metering. Revenue-quality bidirectional metering is provided at the Point of Interconnection, owned, installed, tested and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and sealed at all times.
7.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer provides, at its cost, the provisions for the Company's RTU and makes available the analog and status points that TCS-02 requires. Live telemetry at the System Operations Center is a condition of permission to operate, and any loss of telemetry after permission to operate is reported and remedied as TCS-02 provides.
ARTICLE 8 — OPERATION
8.1 Operating representatives. The Company's operating representative is the System Operations Center. The Interconnection Customer's operating representative is the Corwyn Office Complex property management office, reachable at all times at (612) 555-0827. Each Party gives the other its operating notices through these representatives.
8.2 Loss of the utility source. On any loss of the utility source at the Point of Interconnection, the Facility shall cease to energize within 2.0 seconds.
8.3 Disconnection by the Company. The Company may open the POI recloser and keep the Facility disconnected for a system emergency, for work on its distribution system, on loss of telemetry, or where the Facility fails to meet this Agreement, with notice to the Interconnection Customer where practicable.
8.4 Reconnection. After the Company has opened the POI recloser, the Facility is placed back in parallel only on the release of the System Operations Center.
8.5 Clearances. On the Company's request the Interconnection Customer opens and padlocks the Facility's disconnects identified in Exhibit B for a clearance and keeps them open until the Company releases the clearance.
8.6 Planned outages. The Interconnection Customer gives the System Operations Center five (5) business days' notice of any planned outage of the Facility longer than one day.
8.7 Changes. The Interconnection Customer makes no change to the Facility's equipment or settings without the Company's written consent under Article 12.
ARTICLE 9 — MAINTENANCE AND RECORDS
9.1 The Interconnection Customer maintains the Facility in accordance with the Standards and the manufacturers' instructions.
9.2 The Interconnection Customer tests the Facility's protective functions on a schedule not longer than that of comparable Company equipment and makes the records available to the Company on request (DPS-07 §6.4).
9.3 The Interconnection Customer keeps operating and maintenance records for the Facility for the term of this Agreement and makes them available to the Company on request.
ARTICLE 10 — PAYMENT
10.1 The Interconnection Customer pays for the Company's Facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement and Tariff §12.5.
10.2 Invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date. Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
ARTICLE 11 — LIABILITY AND INSURANCE
11.1 Each Party is responsible for the facilities it owns under this Agreement.
11.2 The Interconnection Customer indemnifies the Company against third-party claims arising from the operation of the Facility, except to the extent caused by the Company's negligence.
11.3 During the term the Interconnection Customer maintains commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and provides a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request.
ARTICLE 12 — AMENDMENTS
12.1 No term of this Agreement may be modified or waived except by an instrument in writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.
12.2 Changes to the capacity or the Point of Interconnection are governed by DIS §7. Other changes to the Facility are made by change order under Section 12.1.
ARTICLE 13 — NOTICES
13.1 Notices under this Agreement are in writing and are delivered by hand, by certified mail, or by e-mail with confirmation of receipt.
13.2 To the Company: DER Program Office — Contracts, Alleniom Utilities, 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA; der.program@alleniom.com; (612) 555-0100.
13.3 To the Interconnection Customer: Corwyn Realty Partners, attention Director of Property Operations, 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR; (612) 555-0827.
13.4 Operating notices under Article 8 pass between the operating representatives named in Section 8.1.
ARTICLE 14 — SIGNATURES
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the dates set forth below, this Agreement being effective as of the date last executed.
ALLENIOM UTILITIES
By: /s/ Dana Whitcomb
Name: Dana Whitcomb
Title: Vice President, Distribution Operations
Date signed: 09/12/2024
CORWYN REALTY PARTNERS
By: /s/ Nadia Ferreira-Holt
Name: Nadia Ferreira-Holt
Title: Director of Property Operations
Date signed: 09/10/2024
Executed in two counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and both of which together constitute one and the same instrument. Filed with the DER Program Office — Contracts, Alleniom Utilities.
EXHIBIT A — POINT OF INTERCONNECTION
Feeder ALN-072, 13.2 kV, three-phase. The Company's POI recloser and revenue meter RM-0629 are on the Company's pole at the north lot. The Interconnection Customer's 13.2 kV primary conductors run from the Point of Interconnection to primary switch PSW-1 and step-up transformer T-1 in the equipment yard.
EXHIBIT B — FACILITY AND INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
B.1 Generating equipment. Five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, INV-C1 to INV-C5, 140 kW (ac) each at 480 V, three-phase, one on each of canopies C1 to C5; 700 kW (ac) in all. The inverters provide the interconnection protective functions by their certified functions (DIS Table 5-1, Category 2) and operate at the IEEE 1547-2018 Category III default settings and constant power factor 1.00 unless the Company directs otherwise in writing.
B.2 Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities. Inverter ac disconnects AD-C1 to AD-C5, one beside each inverter; PV switchboard SWBD-PV with five 225 A inverter breakers and a 1,200 A main breaker; step-up transformer T-1, 750 kVA, 13.2 kV grounded wye to 480Y/277 V; primary switch PSW-1 with current-limiting fuses; the 13.2 kV primary conductors from PSW-1 to the Point of Interconnection.
B.3 Monitoring. The PV monitoring cabinet DAS-1 is the Interconnection Customer's own monitoring and is not part of the Company's telemetry.

=== ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex_Executed_Agreement.docx ===
INTERCONNECTION SERVICE AGREEMENT
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex · Rev Final · Date 09/12/2024 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts
Agreement No.: ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex
Project: Corwyn Office Complex PV
Application No.: PXA-2023-0629
This Interconnection Service Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (the "Company"), and Corwyn Realty Partners, with offices at 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR (the "Interconnection Customer"), each a "Party" and together the "Parties." This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.
RECITALS
WHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2023-0629, on 07/11/2023, for a 700 kW (ac) photovoltaic generating facility on five parking canopies at the Corwyn Office Complex, to be interconnected to the Company's distribution system on Feeder ALN-072;
WHEREAS, the Company completed its review of the application under the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and approved the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in this Agreement;
WHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms part of the terms of interconnection service under this Agreement;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Company's filed tariff (the "Tariff") and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the "DIS").
1.2 "Facility" means the generating facility described in Exhibit B: the five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, one on each of the five parking canopies, together with the Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B.
1.3 "Point of Interconnection" or "POI" means the point on Feeder ALN-072 at which the Facility connects to the Company's distribution system, at the Company's POI recloser in the north lot. The point of common coupling coincides with the Point of Interconnection.
1.4 "Company's Facilities" means the POI recloser, the remote terminal unit (RTU) and revenue meter RM-0629 described in Article 5.
1.5 "Permission to Operate" means the Company's written permission for parallel operation of the Facility under Article 6.
1.6 "Standards" means the Company standards identified in Section 4.1.
ARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY
2.1 Project designation. Corwyn Office Complex PV (Application PXA-2023-0629).
2.2 Interconnection Customer. Corwyn Realty Partners.
2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation on five parking canopies over the surface lots beside the parking structure.
2.4 Capacity. 700 kW (ac), export at the Point of Interconnection.
2.5 Feeder. ALN-072, 13.2 kV.
2.6 Material terms. The capacity and the Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement (Tariff §12.6; DIS §7).
ARTICLE 3 — TERM
3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 09/12/2024, the date on which the last of the Parties executed it.
3.2 Term. This Agreement remains in force from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.
3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality and dispute resolution survive any termination of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 4 — STANDARDS
4.1 The Facility shall be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated and maintained in conformity with DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time.
4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency, the following order governs: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the Standards; (iii) the body of this Agreement and its Exhibits.
ARTICLE 5 — INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
5.1 Company's Facilities. The Company provides, owns and operates the POI recloser (DPS-07 §4.2), the RTU (TCS-02 §3) and revenue meter RM-0629 with 13.2 kV primary metering at the Point of Interconnection, at the Interconnection Customer's cost under the construction work order.
5.2 Interconnection Customer's facilities. The Interconnection Customer provides, owns and maintains the interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B and the site provisions for the Company's Facilities (equipment pad, primary conductors to the recloser terminals, and the station service and communications entrance for the RTU) as specified in the Company's construction package.
5.3 Access. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company access at all times to the Point of Interconnection, the revenue meter and the Facility's disconnects.
ARTICLE 6 — COMMISSIONING AND PERMISSION TO OPERATE
6.1 Witness test. Before permission to operate, the Company may place the Facility in parallel with its distribution system solely for the witness test of the Facility under the Company's Witness Test & Waiver Procedure, under a Distribution Operations switching order and with the System Operations Center observing. At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.
6.2 Permission to operate. Parallel operation begins only with the Company's written permission to operate, issued once the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted, telemetry is live at the System Operations Center, the witness test is complete, and the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities.
6.3 First parallel operation. The first parallel operation after permission to operate is observed by the System Operations Center with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision (DPS-07 §6.3).
ARTICLE 7 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
7.1 Metering. Revenue-quality bidirectional metering is provided at the Point of Interconnection, owned, installed, tested and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and sealed at all times.
7.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer provides, at its cost, the provisions for the Company's RTU and makes available the analog and status points that TCS-02 requires. Live telemetry at the System Operations Center is a condition of permission to operate, and any loss of telemetry after permission to operate is reported and remedied as TCS-02 provides.
ARTICLE 8 — OPERATION
8.1 Operating representatives. The Company's operating representative is the System Operations Center. The Interconnection Customer's operating representative is the Corwyn Office Complex property management office, reachable at all times at (612) 555-0827. Each Party gives the other its operating notices through these representatives.
8.2 Loss of the utility source. On any loss of the utility source at the Point of Interconnection, the Facility shall cease to energize within 2.0 seconds.
8.3 Disconnection by the Company. The Company may open the POI recloser and keep the Facility disconnected for a system emergency, for work on its distribution system, on loss of telemetry, or where the Facility fails to meet this Agreement, with notice to the Interconnection Customer where practicable.
8.4 Reconnection. After the Company has opened the POI recloser, the Facility is placed back in parallel only on the release of the System Operations Center.
8.5 Clearances. On the Company's request the Interconnection Customer opens and padlocks the Facility's disconnects identified in Exhibit B for a clearance and keeps them open until the Company releases the clearance.
8.6 Planned outages. The Interconnection Customer gives the System Operations Center five (5) business days' notice of any planned outage of the Facility longer than one day.
8.7 Changes. The Interconnection Customer makes no change to the Facility's equipment or settings without the Company's written consent under Article 12.
ARTICLE 9 — MAINTENANCE AND RECORDS
9.1 The Interconnection Customer maintains the Facility in accordance with the Standards and the manufacturers' instructions.
9.2 The Interconnection Customer tests the Facility's protective functions on a schedule not longer than that of comparable Company equipment and makes the records available to the Company on request (DPS-07 §6.4).
9.3 The Interconnection Customer keeps operating and maintenance records for the Facility for the term of this Agreement and makes them available to the Company on request.
ARTICLE 10 — PAYMENT
10.1 The Interconnection Customer pays for the Company's Facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement and Tariff §12.5.
10.2 Invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date. Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
ARTICLE 11 — LIABILITY AND INSURANCE
11.1 Each Party is responsible for the facilities it owns under this Agreement.
11.2 The Interconnection Customer indemnifies the Company against third-party claims arising from the operation of the Facility, except to the extent caused by the Company's negligence.
11.3 During the term the Interconnection Customer maintains commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and provides a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request.
ARTICLE 12 — AMENDMENTS
12.1 No term of this Agreement may be modified or waived except by an instrument in writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.
12.2 Changes to the capacity or the Point of Interconnection are governed by DIS §7. Other changes to the Facility are made by change order under Section 12.1.
ARTICLE 13 — NOTICES
13.1 Notices under this Agreement are in writing and are delivered by hand, by certified mail, or by e-mail with confirmation of receipt.
13.2 To the Company: DER Program Office — Contracts, Alleniom Utilities, 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA; der.program@alleniom.com; (612) 555-0100.
13.3 To the Interconnection Customer: Corwyn Realty Partners, attention Director of Property Operations, 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR; (612) 555-0827.
13.4 Operating notices under Article 8 pass between the operating representatives named in Section 8.1.
ARTICLE 14 — SIGNATURES
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the dates set forth below, this Agreement being effective as of the date last executed.
ALLENIOM UTILITIES
By: /s/ Dana Whitcomb
Name: Dana Whitcomb
Title: Vice President, Distribution Operations
Date signed: 09/12/2024
CORWYN REALTY PARTNERS
By: /s/ Nadia Ferreira-Holt
Name: Nadia Ferreira-Holt
Title: Director of Property Operations
Date signed: 09/10/2024
Executed in two counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and both of which together constitute one and the same instrument. Filed with the DER Program Office — Contracts, Alleniom Utilities.
EXHIBIT A — POINT OF INTERCONNECTION
Feeder ALN-072, 13.2 kV, three-phase. The Company's POI recloser and revenue meter RM-0629 are on the Company's pole at the north lot. The Interconnection Customer's 13.2 kV primary conductors run from the Point of Interconnection to primary switch PSW-1 and step-up transformer T-1 in the equipment yard.
EXHIBIT B — FACILITY AND INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
B.1 Generating equipment. Five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, INV-C1 to INV-C5, 140 kW (ac) each at 480 V, three-phase, one on each of canopies C1 to C5; 700 kW (ac) in all. The inverters provide the interconnection protective functions by their certified functions (DIS Table 5-1, Category 2) and operate at the IEEE 1547-2018 Category III default settings and constant power factor 1.00 unless the Company directs otherwise in writing.
B.2 Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities. Inverter ac disconnects AD-C1 to AD-C5, one beside each inverter; PV switchboard SWBD-PV with five 225 A inverter breakers and a 1,200 A main breaker; step-up transformer T-1, 750 kVA, 13.2 kV grounded wye to 480Y/277 V; primary switch PSW-1 with current-limiting fuses; the 13.2 kV primary conductors from PSW-1 to the Point of Interconnection.
B.3 Monitoring. The PV monitoring cabinet DAS-1 is the Interconnection Customer's own monitoring and is not part of the Company's telemetry.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
TELEMETRY & COMMUNICATIONS STANDARD
Doc no. Rev Date Owner
TCS-02 Rev 1 06/01/2021 Alleniom Standards Engineering
Document title: Telemetry & Communications Standard
Applies to: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities interconnected to the Alleniom Utilities
distribution system within the DER Program scope
Effective date: 06/01/2021
Approving authority: Manager, Standards Engineering
§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
 a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
 b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
 c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
 d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
--- Page 2 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 2Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02
Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.
§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
 a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
 b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
 c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
 d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
 e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).
--- Page 3 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 3Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02
Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.
§4   COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1   Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
 a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
 b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
 c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.
Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2   SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3   Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4   Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.
§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
DIS-01 §3.4.
Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:
 a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;
--- Page 4 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 4Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02
 b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh
cadence required by §6; and
 c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged
bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is
issued.
Compliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is
requested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be
issued to any in-scope DER site until §5 is satisfied.
§6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES
§6.1   Required data points
Each in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to
Alleniom SCADA. Where the site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks or multiple
aggregated facilities behind a common POI, values shall be reported both individually per block
and as a facility total.
Analog values (per site, and per block where applicable):
Point Units Sign convention
Real power, net export at POI kW Export positive
Reactive power, net at POI kVAr Absorbing positive
POI voltage, per phase V —
POI current, per phase A —
Frequency at POI Hz —
Gross generation (per inverter block) kW Generation positive
Auxiliary/parasitic load (where separately metered) kW Load positive
Cumulative energy delivered kWh Export positive
Cumulative energy received kWh Import positive
Ambient / cabinet temperature (RTU health) °C —
Status and diagnostic points:
Point Description
Site online / offline Aggregate operating state of the DER
Inverter/PCS block status Per block: run, standby, fault
Communications heartbeat RTU-to-SCADA path health
Time-sync quality GNSS/NTP discipline status
Configuration version Active RTU configuration identifier
Alarm summary Rolled-up device alarm state
§6.2   Refresh rates
--- Page 5 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 5Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02
Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3   Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4   Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.
§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.
--- Page 6 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 6Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02
§7.6   Physical security
The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.
§7.7   Incident response
The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§7.8   Decommissioning
At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.
End of TCS-02.

--- Page 1 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
DISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD
Doc no. Rev Date Owner
DPS-07 Rev 2 09/15/2023 Alleniom Standards Engineering
Effective date: 09/15/2023
Supersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)
Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering
1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
 IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
 IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
 IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
 ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.
--- Page 2 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 2
 Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
 Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and

34: 5.1 Company's Facilities. The Company provides, owns and operates the POI recloser (DPS-07 §4.2), the RTU (TCS-02 §3) and revenue meter RM-0629 with 13.2 kV primary metering at the Point of Interconnection, at the Interconnection Customer's cost under the construction work order.

Before permission to operate, the Company may place the Facility in parallel with its distribution system solely for the witness test of the Facility under the Company's Witness Test & Waiver Procedure, under a Distribution Operations switching order and with the System Operations Center observing. 39: 6.2 Permission to operate. Parallel operation begins only with the Company's written permission to operate, issued once the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted, telemetry is live at the System Operations Center, the witness test is complete, and the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities.
40: 6.3 First parallel operation. The first parallel operation after permission to operate is observed by the System Operations Center with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision (DPS-07 §6.3).
41: ARTICLE 7 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
42: 7.1 Metering. Revenue-quality bidirectional metering is provided at the Point of Interconnection, owned, installed, tested and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and sealed at all times.

46: 8.2 Loss of the utility source. On any loss of the utility source at the Point of Interconnection, the Facility shall cease to energize within 2.0 seconds.
47: 8.3 Disconnection by the Company. Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.

4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.

DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the

the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection

current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.

TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 5Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02
Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3   Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4   Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.
§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 6Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02
§7.6   Physical security
The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.
§7.7   Incident response
The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§7.8   Decommissioning
At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.
End of TCS-02.

Each combiner circuit consists of '2 x 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu PV wire, 2 kV, and 1/C 4 AWG Cu PV wire, green' routed in the north ladder tray and then 'from the tray down the inverter column to the inverter dc inputs in 2 in. rigid steel conduit,' with stated 'Ampacity at 40 °C, 90 °C column (A): 236.6' (260 A × 0.91). If both combiner output circuits on a canopy share a single 2 in. rigid steel conduit riser down the east-end inverter column (as written in singular on E-301 Rev C): (i) under NEC Table 310.15(C)(1), four current-carrying 4/0 AWG conductors in a single conduit > 24 in. long require an 80% (0.80) adjustment factor, reducing adjusted ampacity to 236.6 A × 0.80 = 189.28 A (< 196.875 A required minimum ampacity under NEC 690.8(B)(1) and < 200 A fuse under NEC 690.9(B)), and (ii) under NEC Chapter 9, Table 1, Table 4, and Table 5, four 1/C 4/0 AWG Cu 2 kV PV wire conductors plus one or two 1/C 4 AWG Cu 2 kV PV wire EGCs (total area 1.62 in² to 2.36 in²) exceed the 40% maximum conduit fill area (1.363 in²) of a single 2 in. rigid steel conduit (3.408 in² internal area). I have updated and verified `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` and OpenProject Work Package `#47` in the **DER Program Backlog Review** project so that all four required scope exclusions, register IDs, dates, entities, and pre-PTO settlement requirements are explicitly included and verified.

---

### 1. Deliverables and Locations

1. **Engineering Review Memorandum (Word Document):**
   - **Path:** `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx`
   - **Addressed To:** Lena Kovalchuk, SOC Shift Supervisor, System Operations Center
   - **Prepared For Signature By:** Reviewing Engineer, P.E., DER Program Office (`Tomás Ibarra, P.E.`, Senior Interconnection Engineer, DER Program Office, Alleniom Utilities)
   - **Record Anchor Date:** `07/14/2025` (`2025-07-14`)
   - **Requested PTO Date Evaluated:** `08/04/2025` (`2025-08-04`)

2. **OpenProject Work Package (`DER Program Backlog Review`, Project ID `3`):**
   - **Work Package ID:** `47`
   - **Subject:** `Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) — PTO Determination and Pre-PTO Settlement Items`
   - **Status Line:** `PXA-2023-0629 (Corwyn Office Complex PV): HOLD_PENDING_PRE_PTO_REMEDIATION (CAN_ISSUE_ON_2025-08-04_UPON_CURE)`
   - **Assignee / Priority / Dates:** `S. Rennick` (Commissioning Coordinator, DER Program Office) · Priority: `High` · Start Date: `2025-07-14` · Due Date: `2025-08-04`

---

### 2. Verified Scope Exclusions (Four Matters Under Separate Review)

Both `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` (Section 2) and OpenProject Work Package `#47` explicitly record the four excluded matters under separate review and confirm that **nothing else is under separate review**:
1. `Installation, configuration, and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (under separate review by SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering)`
2. `POI recloser settings and the protection coordination study behind them (under separate review by Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records)`
3. `The site's queue position (under separate review by Meera Vellanki under the weekly queue reports)`
4. `The system impact study and its conditions (under separate review by Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records)`

---

### 3. Summary of Determination and Items Standing in the Way on the `07/14/2025` Record

- **Posture on the `07/14/2025` Record As-Is (Unconditional Release List as of `07/14/2025`: Empty / Zero — HOLD):**
  Working strictly from the project record as it stands on `07/14/2025`, Permission to Operate (PTO) **cannot issue unconditionally on the unamended `07/14/2025` record**. If Items 1 through 5 below are not resolved before `08/04/2025`, Lena Kovalchuk must **HOLD** PTO on `08/04/2025`.
- **Feasibility for the Requested `08/04/2025` PTO Date (CAN ISSUE on `08/04/2025` Subject to Pre-PTO Cure):**
  Every impediment standing in the way on the `07/14/2025` record (**Items 1 through 5** below) **can be cured and verified before `08/04/2025`** (within the 21 calendar days / 15 business days available between `07/14/2025` and `08/04/2025`, requiring ~3–5 business days of field, configuration, and documentation work). All long-lead prerequisites (`ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex` execution on `09/12/2024`, utility RTU and POI recloser installation/acceptance with no open equipment hold under `OG-17`, no screening or standards-conflict holds under `SRP-3` or `ERP-9`, revenue meter `RM-0629` verification on `07/08/2025`, Vexlar `VX-140C` listing on `CEL-2025-Q2` row 18, Certificate of Conformance `VX-CC-25-0522`, Witness Test `WT-0629-01` under `ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3`, and City of Wrenford Final Approval under Permit `WEP-25-0317` on `07/02/2025`) are already satisfied on the record as of `07/14/2025`. Therefore, **Permission to Operate CAN ISSUE on `08/04/2025` once Corwyn Realty Partners (with Brantley Electric Company) and Alleniom Utilities settle Items 1 through 5 prior to `08/04/2025`:**

1. **Item 1 — Utility RTU Station AC Service (`PP-1` Circuit 1 / `TX-1`) and Inverter Control Power Connected Behind the Open POI Recloser (`E-101 Rev C`; `ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §5.2, §6.1–§6.3, §7.2, §8.3–§8.5`; `TCS-02 §3.1, §3.4, §5(c)`; `DPS-07 §4.2(4), §5.1(b), §6.3`; `WT-0629-01`):**
   - *Action Required:* **Corwyn Realty Partners / Brantley Electric Company** must re-feed the dedicated `120 V, 20 A` RTU station service circuit (and auxiliary supply) from permanent building panel `LP-2` in the parking structure electrical room (independent of the POI recloser and `SWBD-PV`), issue revised `E-101 Rev D`, and obtain City of Wrenford AHJ (`Dolores Achebe`) sign-off under Permit `WEP-25-0317`; **SCADA/EMS Engineering (`Marcus Deele`) & SOC (`Lena Kovalchuk`)** must verify continuous station power and live valid telemetry with the POI recloser open (`3–5 business days`; feasible before `08/04/2025`).
2. **Item 2 — Per-Inverter Telemetry Refresh Rate (`5 min` vs. `≤ 4 s`) on `Monitoring and Communications Schedule E-401 Rev C` (`ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §4.1, §6.2, §7.2`; `TCS-02 §3.3(a), §5(b)–(c), §6.1–§6.3`; `DIS-01 Rev 4 §6`):**
   - *Action Required:* **Corwyn Realty Partners / Brantley Electric Company / Vexlar Energy** must configure `INV-C1..C5` RS-485 port 2 (`COM-RTU`) for `≤ 4 s` analog updates (`≤ 60 s` integrity poll) and issue revised `E-401 Rev D` (restricting `5 min` to cumulative `kWh` and `DAS-1`); **SCADA/EMS (`Marcus Deele`) & SOC (`Lena Kovalchuk`)** must verify `≤ 4 s` refresh cadence at SCADA (`1–2 business days`; feasible before `08/04/2025`).
3. **Item 3 — Utility RTU Enclosure `1.5 kVA` Online UPS (`Corvane OL-1500R`) `4-Hour` Ride-Through Under `20%` Cold-Ambient (`< 10 °C`) / End-of-Life Derating (`TCS-02 §3.4`; `ISA §4.1, §5.2, §7.2`; `E-101 Rev C`; `OL1500R-DS Rev 4`):**
   - *Action Required:* **Corwyn Realty Partners / Brantley Electric Company & SCADA/EMS (`Marcus Deele`)** must verify actual continuous watt load on the POI pole RTU UPS output (confirming no heater on UPS output); if `> 31.0 W` (e.g., `38 W` RTU + `12 W` modem = `50 W` $\rightarrow$ `3.88 h` new / `3.10 h` derated), install an external battery pack or higher-capacity UPS achieving `≥ 4.0 h` derated runtime and update `E-101 Rev D` (`2–4 business days`; feasible before `08/04/2025`).
4. **Item 4 — Canopy DC Column Riser (`2 in. RSC`) Fill & Bundling Derating, and NEC Article 690 Warning Labels (`E-301 Rev C` & `E-101 Rev C`; `NFPA 70 / NEC 2023 §§ 690.8(B)(1), 690.9(B), 690.13(B), 690.31(B)(1), 690.56(C), 310.15(C)(1), Ch. 9 Tables 1, 4, 5`; `WEP-25-0317`):**
   - *Action Required:* **Corwyn Realty Partners / Brantley Electric Company** must confirm/install two separate `2 in. RSC` risers per inverter column (1 per combiner circuit so each retains `236.6 A ≥ 200 A` ampacity and `1.18 in² ≤ 1.363 in²` `40%` fill instead of derating to `189.3 A < 196.9 A` and exceeding `40%` fill at `1.62–2.36 in²`), affix `NEC 690.13(B)` line-and-load warning labels, `NEC 690.31(B)(1)` `WARNING: PHOTOVOLTAIC POWER SOURCE` labels at `≤ 3 m (10 ft)` on DC trays/risers, and the `NEC 690.56(C)` rapid shutdown sign at `SWBD-PV`, issue revised `E-101 Rev D` & `E-301 Rev D`, and obtain City of Wrenford AHJ confirmation if conduit is added; **DER Program Office (`S. Rennick` / `Tomás Ibarra, P.E.`)** must verify revised schedules and field completion (`1–3 business days`; feasible before `08/04/2025`).
5. **Item 5 — Day-of-PTO Live Telemetry Confirmation (`TCS-02 §5(c)`) and SOC-Supervised First Parallel Operation (`ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §6.1–§6.3, §7.2`; `DPS-07 Rev 2 §6.3`; `CX-CW-01 Rev 2`):**
   - *Action Required:* **SOC Shift Supervisor (`Lena Kovalchuk`) & Corwyn Realty Partners (`Nadia Ferreira-Holt`)** must confirm valid live telemetry on the SCADA operator display at the moment of PTO issuance on `08/04/2025` (with the POI recloser open), issue written PTO, and supervise POI recloser closure and first parallel operation under SCADA supervision (executed on `08/04/2025` once Items 1–4 are cured).
